blueprint_refs: CALIBRATION IS SBI (NPE) AND MUST MATCH THE CURRENT HOSP PIPELINE
Train NPE posterior p(θ|x) on the simulated pairs; then condition on x_o, sample posterior, and take posterior mean as optimized_parameters.

evidence.metrics: Calibration loss decreases strongly (~298 -> ~23), but train/val/test losses remain extremely high and unchanged (train_loss=858.48, val_loss=862.25, test_loss=843.16).

calibration-objective-mismatch-gaussian-.error_identification: Despite successful minimization of the calibrator's internal training objective, end-to-end evaluation losses do not improve at all, indicating the calibration objective is not aligned with the simulator-to-metrics pipeline.
calibration-objective-mismatch-gaussian-.root_cause_analysis: The calibrator models q(theta|x) as a diagonal Gaussian with a single-pass conditioning and uses its mean as optimized_theta. This is not equivalent to the intended SBI NPE workflow in the blueprint, and it can learn a miscalibrated mapping that reduces NLL on simulated pairs without producing a theta that minimizes downstream trajectory MSE. Additionally, the network is trained to regress the entire posterior from standardized x without explicit amortized posterior sampling/checks, making it prone to 'good NLL / bad downstream' behavior.
calibration-objective-mismatch-gaussian-.correct_approach: In NPEGaussianCalibrator.fit: (1) replace the diagonal-Gaussian posterior surrogate with a loss/objective directly aligned to the evaluation metric, or (2) implement a closer SBI-like NPE flow using a conditional density estimator that supports sampling and then compute posterior mean from samples at x_o. If SBI libraries are not allowed, approximate NPE more faithfully by: training a conditional normalizing flow or mixture density network (not single Gaussian), and validating by sampling multiple theta from q(theta|x_o), rolling out multiple trajectories, and selecting theta that minimizes validation-style MSE on the observation trajectory summary (train_states[0]). Keep the final selection deterministic and based on the same 7-D flattened x used by evaluation.
calibration-objective-mismatch-gaussian-.key_insight: If the calibrator’s training loss improves but evaluation loss is flat, the inference objective is misaligned; add posterior sampling + simulator-in-the-loop selection or use a richer conditional density model so optimized parameters actually minimize the downstream metric.

blueprint_refs: day_index ... allows non-stationary arrival processes by day/time_step if supported by data
Fit mean admissions per day per disease; optionally bucket day/time_step to capture non-stationarity.

evidence.metrics: Very large occupancy/alive-count errors dominate val_loss (val_loss_per_dim: icu_occupancy=1262.57, total_alive=3106.22). A stationary Poisson + stationary LOS often cannot match time-varying census patterns.

arrival-process-too-stationary-missing-d.error_identification: The simulator likely cannot reproduce changing occupancy/alive dynamics over time, leading to large per-dimension MSE, especially for total_alive and ICU occupancy.
arrival-process-too-stationary-missing-d.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.rollout uses constant per-disease Poisson arrival rates (parameters.arrival_lambda[disease_id]) independent of day/time_step. The blueprint explicitly allows day/time_step as a covariate (e.g., day buckets). Without this, parameters compensate poorly, producing persistent mismatch across trajectories and time.
arrival-process-too-stationary-missing-d.correct_approach: Extend ModelParameters and theta representation to support a small number of day buckets (e.g., 3–7) per disease: arrival_lambda[disease, bucket]. In HospitalFlowModel.rollout, compute bucket index from (day0+t) and use the corresponding lambda. Keep parameter count modest to preserve identifiability and generalization (shared buckets across splits). Update get_parameters_uniform_prior_min_max(), theta_to_parameters(), parameters_to_theta(), and theta_to_named_parameters() accordingly.
arrival-process-too-stationary-missing-d.key_insight: When state trajectories are non-stationary, static arrival parameters will inflate occupancy/alive MSE; add low-dimensional time variation (bucketed rates) before increasing model complexity elsewhere.

blueprint_refs: Prefer empirical discrete distribution over observed initial los_remaining (day_in_hospital==1) to match integer nature.
assign initial los_remaining via calibrated LOS distributions conditional on disease_id and bed_type

evidence.metrics: Large errors in alive counts/occupancy suggest LOS-driven census dynamics are off; current calibrated los_mean values cluster around ~12–14 days but still do not reduce val_loss.

los-distribution-mismatch-geometric-vs-e.error_identification: Census dynamics (occupancy and alive counts) remain far from data even after calibration, indicating LOS sampling is structurally mismatched.
los-distribution-mismatch-geometric-vs-e.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel._sample_los uses a geometric distribution parameterized by mean. Real hospital LOS distributions are typically heavy-tailed and not memoryless, and the blueprint recommends using an empirical discrete distribution of initial los_remaining at admission (day_in_hospital==1) conditional on (disease, bed_type). The geometric assumption can distort the discharge hazard shape, producing systematic census errors that parameter tuning cannot fix.
los-distribution-mismatch-geometric-vs-e.correct_approach: Replace geometric LOS sampling with an empirical discrete sampler per (disease_id, bed_type) built from train data admissions (patients with day_in_hospital==1). Implement: (1) during data load or in a new preprocessing step (using existing parsed patients), build observed support values and probabilities for initial los_remaining by group; (2) store them inside the model (not as learnable neural params) or as calibratable simplex parameters with a small capped support; (3) in _sample_los, sample from this discrete distribution. Keep max_los consistent with observed support.
los-distribution-mismatch-geometric-vs-e.key_insight: If occupancy/alive errors persist after calibrating LOS means, the LOS distribution shape is wrong; model LOS with empirical discrete support at admission to match discharge dynamics.

blueprint_refs: Observation x_o (single-trajectory): use ONLY train_states[0] (trajectory_id=0) as the observation.
Evaluation: using optimized_parameters, evaluate on ALL trajectories from train/val/test

evidence.metrics: train_loss and val_loss are both extremely high and nearly equal (858.48 vs 862.25), suggesting parameters learned from a single observation are not informative enough to generalize, and/or calibration is ineffective.

single-trajectory-observation-overfits-a.error_identification: Learned parameters do not improve training or validation trajectory fit, indicating the single-trajectory observation provides weak identifiability for the current parameterization and/or inference method.
single-trajectory-observation-overfits-a.root_cause_analysis: Even though the blueprint mandates using train_states[0] as x_o, the simulator’s current parameterization (stationary arrivals + geometric LOS + single Gaussian posterior) likely makes many parameters weakly identifiable from a single trajectory, causing posterior collapse to average-ish values that don't fit any split well.
single-trajectory-observation-overfits-a.correct_approach: Keep x_o construction per blueprint, but improve identifiability by changing simulator structure (time-bucket arrivals; empirical LOS) and by adding simulator-in-the-loop selection at x_o (sample multiple theta candidates from learned q(theta|x_o) and choose theta that minimizes MSE on x_o’s trajectory summary). This preserves the blueprint’s single-observation rule while making the chosen theta actually fit the observation and transfer better.
single-trajectory-observation-overfits-a.key_insight: When constrained to a single observation trajectory, improve structural identifiability and add a final simulator-based selection step; otherwise inference can converge to parameters that satisfy the density model but not the trajectory metric.

blueprint_refs: optional mortality/early-exit is disabled by default unless strongly supported by data

evidence.metrics: Alive-count MSE is very large, but this is more likely driven by arrivals/LOS mismatch than mortality; still, mortality is implicitly fixed to always alive for new admissions.

missing-mortality-toggle-explicitly-off-.error_identification: Mortality is effectively disabled (good), but the implementation removes patients only via LOS and checks p.is_alive without any explicit mechanism toggle, which can complicate future extensions and debugging of alive counts.
missing-mortality-toggle-explicitly-off-.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.rollout filters roster with `p.los_remaining > 0 and p.is_alive`, but there is no explicit mortality parameter/toggle in ModelParameters; new patients are always created with is_alive=True. This matches the default-off blueprint intent but is implicit rather than explicit, making it harder to verify alignment when data contains is_alive fields.
missing-mortality-toggle-explicitly-off-.correct_approach: Add an explicit mortality toggle/parameter in ModelParameters (default off / zero hazard) only if needed, and ensure initialization from data preserves is_alive. Also add a short invariant/debug hook (optional) to verify that is_alive stays True when mortality is disabled, to avoid accidental changes affecting alive summaries.
missing-mortality-toggle-explicitly-off-.key_insight: When a mechanism is 'disabled by default', keep it explicitly represented as a toggle with a no-op default so future changes don’t silently alter evaluation-relevant summaries.
